name: LM6171 / LM6172
tagline: National's 100 MHz video op-amp (3600 / 3000 V/µs). Rollers call it neutral and detailed, but opinion is split.

lineage.note: Macromodels v4.30 (1996-04-18) include LM6171A/B and LM6172; VIP3 process. Datasheet LM6171 DS012336.
SNOS745 (LM6171) and SNOS792 (LM6172). PCN 20241217001.1 adds BICOMHD die and TI Mexico assembly for LM6172.

part_numbers.note: Generic single; datasheet SNOS745. TI product page live; A grade Active.
National A-grade DIP-8 / SOIC-8 (MicroSim symbols); model gives 3 mV max Vos.
Lead-free A-grade SOIC and reel; AIMX/NOPB is the PDN replacement.
B-grade SOIC; discontinued by PDN 20230906005.3 (DigiKey: obsolete).
B-grade DIP-8, listed obsolete by distributors. Model gives 6 mV max Vos.
Dual DIP-8 used by rollers; retailed by Bispa and eleshop.jp.
Dual SOIC-8 and reel; may carry VIP3 or BICOMHD die after 2024.
Military and space-grade versions with TI product pages; LM6172NAB/EM reportedly listed.
Bare-die version with its own TI datasheet; not a hobbyist part.

key_specs.value: Bipolar VFB, unity-gain stable (VIP3; BICOMHD from 2024)

reputation.summary: A cult rolling pick with split opinion. nabe ranked the LM6172 'straightest', ahead of the OP275; diyAudio posters call it very detailed and neutral. Some JP listeners call it a wasted purchase with light bass; Head-Fi is mixed. The Shanling H1.1 DAC uses LM6171s, per Soomal. No ASR measurements. All reports predate the 2024 LM6172 die change.
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in Chu-Moy/CMoy headphone amps
Headphone output stage (Shanling H1.1 uses LM6171)
DAC I/V or output stages in DIY builds
Video, high-speed paths, ADC drivers (original target)
caveats: Layout- and stability-sensitive ('cranky' per AMB and Head-Fi); needs tight decoupling; risky in sockets.
Not beginner-friendly; results depend heavily on the surrounding circuit.
Opinion split, bass reports conflict; the DiyEden/Soomal CMoy translation wrongly calls it FET-input.
From 2025 LM6172 stock may carry the new BICOMHD die; reviews describe VIP3 silicon.
No vendor audio-THD figures; a CMoy noise-floor ranking (UIUC P406 report) is unconfirmed.

counterfeit_notes: No LM6171/LM6172 fakes reported. Rollers want DIP LM6172IN and LM6171BIN; Bispa and eleshop.jp retailed genuine stock. Check logo, date code and /NOPB marking. Since 2025, NiPdAu leads or a different pin-1 mark may mean genuine new-process parts.

part_numbers_affected: LM6172 family ('select devices'; orderables not listed here)
silicon_changes.identification: Datasheet SNOS792E. Mexico vs Melaka assembly differs in lead finish (matte Sn vs NiPdAu), compounds, pin-1 notch vs dimple; shows site, not fab. Risk: 2025+ date codes.
silicon_changes.summary: TI qualified FFAB (Freising) with BICOMHD (FR-BIP-1, 200 mm) for the LM6172 beside National's DL-LIN VIP3 (150 mm), with a changed die and added TI Mexico assembly. Part of TI's 150 mm exit. First ship 2025-03-18. One part number now covers two silicon builds.

spec_deltas.after: TI Melaka or TI Mexico (added), with different lead finish, mold/mount compound and pin-1 mark

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. A new process can change noise, distortion, slew and phase margin. All listening reports predate 2025 (VIP3 silicon).
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: redesigned die on a different process; SNOS792E changes unknown; socketed stability margins may differ.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN confirmed earlier; LM6171 coverage unconfirmed. Current datasheet text still says VIP III; check SNOS792E history.

part_numbers_affected: LM6171BIN (listed obsolete by distributors; not confirmed in the PDN text)
silicon_changes.identification: Grade discontinuance, not a silicon change. A grade (LM6171AIM/NOPB, AIMX/NOPB) remains Active; any B-grade part sold now is old stock.
silicon_changes.summary: TI PDN 20230906005.3 ('Discontinuance of Select Devices') includes LM6171BIM, replaced pin-to-pin by LM6171AIMX/NOPB. DigiKey lists LM6171BIM/NOPB obsolete. The A grade stays Active. SNOS745D (Nov 2023) coincides; its changes were not seen.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None: B and A grades are selections of the same die.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: grade discontinuance only; the A-grade replacement has the same pinout.
silicon_changes.verification: PDN listing and DigiKey status seen; PDN PDF not read; LM6171BIN inclusion unconfirmed.

revision_history.changes: Library dated 18 April 1996: 'Models added: LM6172' (3 mV, 100 MHz, 2.3 mA, 3000 V/µs); LM6171A/B (3600 V/µs, 2.5 mA, 90 dB) present.
National LM6171 datasheet, pre-2011; TI gives original date May 1998. Editions undated; continued as SNOS745.
Implied by Rev C; probably National format with TI number after 2011. Low confidence.
Header 'SNOS745C – MAY 1998 – REVISED MARCH 2013' (Mouser, Octopart). Changes unknown.
Restyled title 'LM6171 High-Speed, Low-Power, Low-Distortion Voltage Feedback Amplifier'. Changes unknown; coincides with PDN 20230906005.3.
Header 'SNOS792C – MAY 2004 – REVISED SEPTEMBER 2004' (Octopart LM6172IN). Changes unknown.
Header 'SNOS792D – MAY 1999 – REVISED MARCH 2013' (RS, PUC-Rio); probably TI's 2013 reformat.
Per PCN 20241217001.1: FFAB BICOMHD die and TI Mexico assembly added; title restyled. Electrical changes unknown.

open_questions: What changed in SNOS792E's electrical tables with the BICOMHD die?
Which orderables does PCN 20241217001.1 cover (PDIP, QML)? Does VIP3 die keep shipping in parallel?
Why was SNOS745D issued in Nov 2023? Any LM6171 fab PCN? Is SNOS792C's 'MAY 2004' header real?
National DS number and edition dates for LM6172; lit numbers of LM6172QML, QML-SP, -MDE datasheets?
Lifecycle of all orderables, especially DIP; LM6172 noise, output current and supply range against the datasheet?

claims_confirmed: Current LM6171 datasheet SNOS745D, revised November 2023, with hyphenated title (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm6171.pdf).
Current LM6172 datasheet SNOS792E, 'MAY 1999 – REVISED DECEMBER 2024' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm6172.pdf).
SNOS792D 'MAY 1999 – REVISED MARCH 2013' on the PUC-Rio mirror (https://www.maxwell.vrac.puc-rio.br/21708/21708_4.PDF).
SNOS792C 'MAY 2004 – REVISED SEPTEMBER 2004' on Octopart under LM6172IN (https://datasheet.octopart.com/LM6172IN-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-12525018.pdf).

PCN 20241217001.1 (18 Dec 2024, first ship 18 Mar 2025): FFAB BICOMHD 200 mm beside DL-LIN VIP3 150 mm, changed die, TI Mexico assembly, SNOS792D→E (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/6025/PCN20241217001.1.pdf).
TI pages exist for LM6171, LM6172, LM6172QML, LM6172QML-SP and LM6172IM/NOPB (https://www.ti.com/product/LM6172QML-SP; https://www.ti.com/product/LM6172/part-details/LM6172IM/NOPB).
Carnegie Observatories mirror holds an old-style LM6172 datasheet (https://instrumentation.obs.carnegiescience.edu/ccd/parts/LM6172.pdf).
refuted_claims: 'No die change or PCN' is wrong: PCN 20241217001.1 (18 Dec 2024) adds FFAB BICOMHD 200 mm silicon with a changed die; SNOS792D→SNOS792E.
An empty silicon_changes list is wrong; the PCN is a same-part-number, different-silicon hazard.
'LM6171 has no TI literature number' is wrong: it is SNOS745 (SNOS745C Mar 2013, SNOS745D Nov 2023).
The old title 'LM6171 High Speed Low Power...' belongs to SNOS745C and earlier; the current title is hyphenated.
The current LM6172 revision is SNOS792E, revised December 2024.
PCN 20250730004.1 (DL-LIN-2 EXCAL2 150 mm to RFAB TIB 300 mm, Cu wire 0.96→0.8 mil, die 10.5→7.5 mil) surfaced but does not cover LM6171/LM6172.
corrections: Added LM6171 lit number SNOS745: rev C (May 1998, revised Mar 2013) and D (Nov 2023); symlink set to rev D.
LM6172 current revision set to SNOS792E (Dec 2024); added SNOS792C (Sep 2004, Octopart LM6172IN).
Added PCN 20241217001.1 silicon change: VIP3 150 mm to BICOMHD 200 mm, changed die, Mexico assembly (Sn vs NiPdAu, notch vs dimple), first ship 18 Mar 2025.
Added old-revision mirrors: Mouser, Octopart, PUC-Rio, datasheetcatalog, AG Electronica, eecart, alldatasheet, DigiKey HTML.
Added LM6171AIM/NOPB, LM6171BIM/NOPB, LM6172IM/NOPB, LM6172QML, LM6172QML-SP, LM6172-MDE.
Lineage names VIP3 and the 2024 BICOMHD transfer; TI header dates (May 1998, May 1999) postdate the 1996 macromodels.
National.com legacy datasheet entries downgraded to low confidence.
LM6171 key specs (3600 V/µs, 100 MHz, 2.5 mA) also sourced to the TI datasheet.
Counterfeit notes: 2025+ date codes, NiPdAu leads or a new pin-1 mark may be genuine new-process parts.
